lines.english: "Good morning!"
"Good morning."
"Good morning."
"It's been a while, Ogiso-chan! You've become even cuter than last time."
"Thank you very much. Here, have some refreshments."
"That professional smile of yours is also only getting better and better…"
"Huh? You can tell? Hmm… I guess I still have a long way to go."
"And little by little you will start losing that pure heart of yours. In the beginning, your face would get bright red as you'd get mad at me. Though that too was also cute in its own way."
"You keep calling her cute every single time you see her, Yamaguchi-san. No wonder she's gone numb to it."
"If you keep repeating the same phrase, it won't have any impact."
"Shut up, you two. Ah, come to think of it, I heard you were at it again for the first time in a while, Ogiso-chan."
"Eh? At it?"
"I'm talking about your third appearance in Studio Troy. You're having a live concert next weekend, aren't you?"
"Oh no, why do you know about that? It's just a minor event in a tiny studio."
"I keep telling you I'm your biggest fan, Ogiso-chan. That's why I know every single thing about you."
"W-Wow…"
"…Don't actually take a step back from me."
"Isn't their drummer Sugita-san? You know, the one with an exclusive contract with us. That place is his home stage."
"And he heard the news from the master of that place. He told us all about it yesterday."
"He heard the news… that I was going to appear?"
"He said that the legendary songstress is appearing on stage for the first time in a year, so make sure everyone in the industry comes to see."
"…!? I-I'm not legendary! I'm just a backup singer…"
"But look, it even says so on the leaflet… This thing is being spread around far and wide, you know?"
"…Tomo."
"I've heard a lot more too about the Ogiso Setsuna Legend. For example, during her university festival, she broke the record with her performance."
"That was during high school… not university."
"Or how she suddenly started singing out loud during her interview."
"That's because… he asked about my hobbies."
"That's not all. You're famous for singing during a presentation too. Unbelievably well, I might add."
"That's because… they asked me which song I was talking about."
"Wouldn't you usually just play a recording in cases like that?"
"I forgot to bring a recording… but going to fetch one would take too much time, so I had no choice."
"I'd believe you if it had happened only once or twice."
"Uuu…"
"I know what this is. Ogiso-chan's looked like an intellectual ever since she left Houjou, but her true calling is in expressing her feelings."
"I can't… deny that that's a part of me."
"Why would such a legendary songstress bother doing public relations work? Normally, you'd be better off debuting as a singer."
"Because I don't have the skill to become a professional. This is nothing more than a mere hobby… And stop calling me a legendary songstress."
"But I'm sure you'd sell well…"
"Frankly speaking, that goes for more than just her singing."
"I can't deny that… To be honest, Ogiso-chan is the type who's either incredibly popular with women, or incredibly envied by them."
"E-Eeh!? Motoko-san, please, give me a break!"
"Ah, it's fine, it's fine. I'm one of the ones who like you… for the most part. If you were to debut, I would cheer you on."
"I won't and I can't… After all, I know what true geniuses are like. I couldn't possibly walk the path of music."
"Oh, how interesting. The genius who made the legendary songstress give up. Is that person a professional now?"
"She's beyond a professional…"
"Kitami-san is here! Everyone stand by."
"Alright! Let's give it our all today!"
"Yes, I look forward to working with everyone!"
"Same goes for me."
"Same goes for me."
"Yep. We must always give it our best, no matter what it is."
"I'll give that 75 points… out of a 1000."
"Then stop applauding. It reeks of sarcasm."
"I wouldn't be able to play a performance this half-assed even if I tried. I'm impressed, in a way."
"Kazusa, you didn't get any sleep last night either, did you? Most of your food is still left there too. I'm starting to get sick of this jet lag excuse."
"Shut up."
"I'm not going to ask what the matter is, because it's not like I don't have an idea."
"…There is a reason. Nothing in this country fits me."
"Well, you can keep telling yourself that. But you know… you lived and breathed the air of this land for almost two decades before leaving."
"Back then I had no other place to live, so I wasn't even aware that it didn't fit me."
"Now it's different… This isn't the place for me to live. It's nothing but one of the countless countries in the world."
"Even then, you were the one who decided, you know? You chose to come to Japan, to play here."
"I know that… so I'll quickly get it over with and quickly return home. To my true homeland."
"But if you go on like this… you won't be able to play anything worth listening to, for anyone."
"I'll get better… There's plenty of time until the concert. I'll slowly build up something good."
"I'm praying that that's the case. I cannot bear seeing my fellow countrymen being disappointed in my own daughter."
"…I want to concentrate. Can you get out?"
"Fine then. Do your best… at least enough to sound impressive to amateurs."
"Mind your own business!"
"Ah, by the way, I have business tonight, so I won't return to the hotel. My phone will probably be off too."
"This again? You've been out fooling around without restraint ever since you came back to Japan."
"This is, after all, my first long term stay in Japan in a long time. I have to take the opportunity to catch up with old friends."
"…I'm just happy you're still at it, at your age."
"Unlike you, I have a lot of friends."
"You have a lot of men too."
"Unlike you, I don't have feelings for them."
"It looks like it's about to snow today. Make sure to keep yourself warm tonight… Even if you can't sleep, at least lie down and close your eyes."
"Don't act like my mother."
"…Right, see you later."
"Come on, I need to pull myself together. What am I even doing…?"
"Miss?"
"Miss, hey Miss!"
"…Eh? W-What?"
"…We're here now. Onjuku Imperial Hotel."
"Ah…"
"Are you okay? You seem under the weather."
"Ah, no, I'm fine. It's just that I have cold chills even though my body feels warm."
"…That doesn't sound fine at all. Should I drive you to the hospital?"
"We're at the hotel, so it's okay… Thanks for your concern."
"Don't mention it… Huh? Have I seen you somewhere…?"
"How much for the fare?"
"Haah…"
"Um, excuse me? I'm Itakura from Shandy Editing of The Orient Magazine."
"You are Touma Kazusa-san, correct? Could I ask you a few questions, if it's alright?"
"Sorry, but I'm tired."
"It'll take no more than two or three minutes. It won't be any bother."
"I just said I'm tired…"
"You say that every day. Come on, you could at least give us a few moments."
"Then I'll go ahead and begin. Thank you very much."
"…Right."
"Actually, I want to shift away from the piano this time, and instead ask about your fashion, Touma-san."
"Huh?"
"I see you're wearing a primarily black and stylish get-up that goes well with your beautiful long black hair. It's become the talk of the town among women your age."
"No… What are you talking about?"
"Go ahead and tell me everything about… all the brands you use, make-up tips, and your approach to outfit coordination."
"…I don't understand at all. What kind of interview is this?"
"Oh and also, we'll send a request at a later date, but we look forward to doing a photoshoot with you too. We're going to have you on our front page!"
"You can bring whatever attire you want with you, or you could just leave it to us to pick the outfit… Ah, I'm sorry for changing the subject."
"Hey…"
"Yes? What is it? Let's not keep anything hidden! Tell me everything."
"I really want to be left alone today. I'm seriously tired…"
"In that case, instead of standing out here, how about we sit down at the hotel cafe?"
"Ah! Or if you haven't eaten yet, we could go to a place that serves food. I can guide you to countless places nearby."
"Aah! There is no need to worry. Our company will of course stand the bill. So please follow me…"
"…uch me."
"Yes?"
"Don't… touch me!"
"Kyah!?"
"W-W-Wha…What are you doing, all of a sudden!?"
"N-No, I'm sor…"
"No matter how you look at it, that's going too far… Ah, ouch, it hit my knee…"
"Ah, aah…"
"There are things you can and can't do… Just because I'm in a weaker position doesn't mean that…"
"Ah, w-wait! Touma-san, Touma-san!"
"Wait! It's cowardly to run away! Wait for me!"
"Besides… you dropped your bag."
"Haah, haah, haah… ngh… haah…"
"Why…?"
"Why does this have to happen to me…?"
"All of this… is his fault…!"
"Ah…"
The moment I leave the Kaiousha Building, I notice the ground is wet.
According to the weather forecast, it will either rain or snow tonight, but it seems like the weather itself is doing its best to contradict that.
The raindrops that fall upon my face are painfully cold. …This is sleet.

People with umbrellas wear sullen expressions as they walk about the streets with a quickened pace. The sleet means they need the cover of umbrellas unlike on regular snowy days, though they're still vulnerable to slipping on the snow underfoot.
I stare absentmindedly at this scenery for a while, but it seems that the sleet isn't going to weaken any time soon, let alone subside completely.
…While I'm at it, I thought that going back to the third floor to retrieve my foldable umbrella was too much trouble.
"Haah…"
Even so, trying to endure the current situation without doing anything isn't going to get me anywhere, so I had no choice but to sluggishly go back.
If this were a usual Friday, I would have dashed to the station before I could even dawdle or hesitate about something like this.
After all, if this were a usual Friday… I would have been much more motivated to return to my apartment.
I'm so caught up in these pointless thoughts that…
I hurriedly pressed the answer button on my cell phone without even checking the caller.
I believed it to be Setsuna…
"H-Hello!?"
"…Hello?"
But almost as if ridiculing my enthusiasm…
Rather than a laugh, all I can hear from the other side of the line is the sound of the city streets. Just like the sound coming from my end of the line.
"Who am I speaking to?"
After that, I finally check the number on the display…
The display shows it's a payphone, something I haven't seen on the caller screen in a few years.
"Hello…? Hello?"
"Setsuna…?"
"Ah…"
The reason I asked that name first was for safety…
Because had I uttered the name of the person I most suspected and been wrong, there's no telling what would happen…
Even as I'm receiving a silent call, overwhelmed with impatience and unease, I still find myself acting in a sly and cool-headed manner, which makes me dislike myself even more.
"Is that you… Kazusa?"
"…Haruki."
"…! What the hell are you doing?"
"Weren't you the one who said we'd never meet again…? Why would you call me…?"
My voice is shaking terribly, but not from the cold.
"Weren't you never going to come near me ever again…? Since I have a history with you…!?"
"I'm not near you… I'm only calling you, aren't I?"
"It's the same thing, you idiot…"
"Don't call me an idiot… Don't treat me like I belong to you."
"Why did you call me, Kazusa…? Is it fun for you to torment me like this?"
No, no…
"That's the first conclusion you come to without even asking…? You don't even have a fragment of kindness in you, do you?"
"Ah, fine already, my bad. So what is it? Keep it short, please."
I never wanted to talk to her in this way. Even if I'm to tell her these things, I wanted to do it in a very different way.
"If you want me to keep it short, I can explain it with one sentence… Go disappear, you idiot."
"Don't call me an idiot… Don't treat me that way."
"Hey, what's the matter, Kazusa?" or "Is there something you want to talk about?"
"You're the worst, you know? …I've had enough."
"I see… goodbye then."
But right now I…
Now that I have promised Setsuna that I'd be waiting for her…
"Sorry for bothering you. This time I won't only never meet you again, but I won't call you either. It's goodbye forever this time."
"Goodby…!"
"Where are you right now?"
Yet why am I afraid of crossing the line at the very end…?
No, what I'm doing is crossing the line.
"I don't know. Where am I?"
"I have no idea what you're talking about."
And Kazusa too continues to speak, even though she just proclaimed that this would be our final goodbye.
Why is she answering me immediately, as if she's anticipating me to respond to her?
"I'm inside a telephone booth for the time being. …Fortunately, it's not cold in here."
"You're outside, right? Are you nearby?"
"Do you think I can answer that given I have no idea where you are?"
"Kaiousha… in Onjuku."
But it's not like there's anything wrong with this.
I'm simply answering her in a professional way. I'm only helping her out a little.
"What a coincidence… I'm also in Onjuku… I think."
"You think? What is that supposed to…"
"I was in front of my hotel at first, but I have no memory of in what direction and how far I walked from there."
"…And?"
The way I'm speaking so calmly right now proves that.
"How can I go back… to the hotel?"
"You can just call a taxi, can't you? …Did you call me just to ask for such an obvious answer?"
…Though I suppose rather than calm, I'm being far too cold. I don't think I'd be able to act like this toward someone I didn't have an interest in.
"The truth is… this number is the only one I remember. What's wrong with me?"
Yet this idiot is mixing strange hints into the conversation.
"My mom's number, the number to the office… and our home number are all saved under my contacts…"
"Hey, what do you mean by that?"
She can call my number, which she knows by heart, but she can't call the other numbers that are saved in her phone's memory.
And her call is from a telephone booth…
"Did your phone… run out of battery?"
"My phone, my phone… Ah, that was also inside with the rest."
"Inside… inside what?"
Something's wrong. Something's happened to Kazusa…
"What happened to it…? I had it on me when I got out of the taxi."
I immediately feel a chill go down my spine. The terrifying omen causes my knees to tremble.
"Don't tell me… Did you lose your phone?"
Normally, this wouldn't be that big of a deal.
"I had it in my pouch along with the rest… I don't tend to walk around with things like that normally, so mom had enough and bought it for me."
"You didn't just lose your phone, but everything…?"
"Yes… My clothes and accessories are all things mom or people from the company bought for me. I mean, I never go out shopping by myself."
"Wait a minute. Calm down!"
I'm the one who's not calm.
"After all, I have no interest in clothes. I have no idea what I should wear. And that fashion journalist wanted to write about me… Is she an idiot or something?"
"Listen to me, Kazusa. Everything should be fine if you take a taxi and return to the hotel."
"Why do I… Why do I have to run away…? I haven't done anything wrong, I haven't…"
And Kazusa seems to have forgotten the reason she called me.
"If you don't want to explain your circumstances, just tell them to take you to the Kaiousha Building. I'm by the entrance over there, so I can…"
"I'm cold, I'm cold, Haruki… but I can't fall asleep. It's reasonable to say I'd die if I fell asleep."
"Where are you? Where are you right now!?"
"I keep telling you that I don't know myself. You never listen to what people have to say, do you?"
"Get it together, Kazusa! Come to your senses and think normally!"
"That's impossible… I feel so feverish. I think this might be around 39°C…"
"Call an ambulance! It's 119 in Japan!"
"Are you stupid…? I can't use an ambulance as a taxi. I read in Kaiou Graph that people doing that is becoming a problem recently, you know?"
"Kazusa!"
It's no use… she really has lost the ability to think straight.
This isn't a situation I can run away from anymore. If I don't do something, she's helpless.
"What can you see nearby? What can you see!?"
Yes, she's helpless. I have no choice but to do something.
"Like I said, I'm in a telephone booth…"
"Concentrate and look! Do you see any distinctive buildings?"
"Ah… there is a Yack, right in front of me."
"How many of those do you think there are in Onjuku?"
Of all the unique landmarks Kazusa could detect in her barely conscious state, she had to pick a world-famous hamburger chain.
And…
"Crap, the call is…"
"Ah…"
The use of the 100 yen coin she paid withーwhether she found it or if she had it in her pocketーhad just run its course.
…A telephone booth and a hamburger restaurant.
I try to narrow her location down with hints so vague they could be straight from an orienteering competition.
"Found you…"
She was right in front of the station.
Actually, thinking about it with a cool head, telephone booths nowadays are so rare that finding one is the hard part.
The amount of people who have regular use of one are so few that even if someone were to sit in one and never leave, no one would care.
"Are you okay?"
Not that there is any point in asking her that.
After all, had this stubborn person been okay, she would never have relied on me… I think.
"Hey, Kazusa…"
"You're late…"
I was only five minutes away from here, but in the end, it took me almost 30 minutes to get here.
Because I had no idea she'd be in such an easy to find place.
There are countless taxis right in front of her, and she could get on a train at any time… But more than anything, there is a map right over here!
"Anyway, stand up. You'll catch a cold if you stay around here."
Though I can't tell her that in this situation, I couldn't say that even if it wasn't Kazusa.
"It's too late… I'm on the verge of getting pneumonia."
"All the more reason to hurry. Come on, grab my hand."
I grab her outreached hand and pull her up.
"…You're heavy."
"…Go to hell."
Because Kazusa is barely exerting any strength, her entire body weight is resting on my arms.
Anyone looking would think she has blacked out from drinking too much.
No one could possibly know that this is the famous Touma Kazusa.
"Anyway, we're moving. Hang in there for a bit."
"Okay…"
Kazusa shows a vague sign of agreement, even though her entire body and voice are still unsteady.
And then she slowly glues herself to my back…
"…Now you listen here."
"You're taking a taxi today. So at least walk that far."
She actually put her hands on my shoulders and tried to ride piggyback.
…Just like that night in Strasbourg.
"Come on, get it together."
"Okay…"
After taking almost ten minutes to get Kazusa to the taxi stand 50 meters away, I finally manage to get her inside the car.
…At this point, I might as well have just given her a piggyback ride.
"Where are you going?"
"Ah, um…"
"Haah, haah, haaah…"
Once Kazusa makes it to her seat, she starts breathing heavily and averts her eyes toward the window, as if she's trying to avoid my gaze.
Even though the window is already wet from the rain, her breath clouds it white, proving just how high her body temperature is.
"…To Minami-Suetsugu, please."
That's why I couldn't ask her.
The name of the hotel that is surely right around the corner.
"Someone dropped it off? Thank goodness…"
I show Kazusa a thumbs up, but she only nods apathetically.
"And the contents… Yes, that's right. There should be two credit cards."
The person telling me that Kazusa's belongings are fine is the only employee in the Japanese branch of Touma Youko Office.

When I called Hamada-san about the number to their office, he pestered me with questions about whether I'm up for the exclusive coverage after all. Once I called the office, this woman who seemed to be about to head home answered.
"Her cell phone and her purse."
No other company than Touma Youko Office would so easily trust a young man like me claiming to be calling in Kazusa's name.
…I do think they should worry about security a little more, though.
"Her cash… Huh? Only 1430 yen?"
"…Yes, it seems she never had more on hand. There's no mistaking it."
Kazusa gives a thumbs up to let me know everything is in order.
How careless can an alleged adult be…?
"Eh? Oh, yes. I'll make sure to tell her as well. Um… I think she's on her way back to the hotel right now."
"Ah, no! It's okay! I'll call you back myself. I think I'll do so tomorrow or the day after that."
"Yes, yes… well then, thank you very much."
"Haah…"
"Good for you, Haruki. They found all the lost items."
"By the way, do you have any food? You were on the phone for so long I started to feel hungry."
At this point, there are so many mistakes in what she's saying I don't even know where to start correcting her…
"I know! I like that thing. Make that thing."
"What do you mean, 'that thing'? Stop speaking in riddles like an old man."
"You know, that thing. Vongole porridge. It tastes awful, but it's the best you can make."
"I can make dishes that require a bit more skill now…"
"It can be prepared quickly, so it'll do."
"No, it takes about the same amount of time…"
"Stop being so stubborn and make it already. Vongole porridge. I'm dying from hunger."
"You were dying from the cold just earlier…"
"Shut up. You always have to worry about every little detail…"
"Alright, alright already… Then wait twenty minutes."
She asked if I had "any food," but it's curious how she's so set on this specific dish.
Regardless, since I'm not short on ingredients or unsure about my seasoning, I put the pot on the stove and light it up.
More importantly, she's doing better than I expected. She's around 37.7°C, so it's not exactly high. But as of now, Kazusa's health comes first…
What am I saying?
Before I know it, I've done it again.
She said "We'll never meet again", "Go disappear, you idiot", "It's goodbye forever this time"…
I swore that I would never get close to Kazusa for Setsuna's sake…
"…I've prepared some pajamas for you. Change into them as I make the food… The bathroom is that way."
"These are for women."
"Are they… Setsuna's?"
"…Well."
"…Of course they are. Why would you muddle your words about it?"
"Sorry."
"It's not like I don't know. I know this room is a place that belongs to Setsuna. …I'll be borrowing it for a bit."
"Put the clothes you take off in the basket. I'll dry them off for tomorrow."
"Mind your own business."
She knows, huh?
I see… She knows.
She knows that I purposefully gave her Setsuna's clothes, the true reason behind it, and why I was lost for words just now.
She knows everything…
"…Sip…"
"How is it…?"
"Kazusa…?"
"…It tastes bad after all. This isn't something you should serve to people."
"You were the one who said you wanted it."
"Only to remember how bad it tasted."
"Keep talking."
"Hmph."
As expected, Kazusa has only bad things to say.
After all, her reaction is identical to back then.
"…Sip…"
That day…
Just like today, Kazusa collapsed, and I was in the kitchen of the Touma household…
"Setsuna taught me this dish."
"Come to think of it… that's right."
"…Did I tell you about it before?"
"Ah…"
It was five years ago when Setsuna taught me how to make this.
Kazusa was in an even worse state than she is today, putting the whole school festival performanceーthat took place only a few days afterーin danger.
Setsuna taught me the recipe over the phone, and I'm certain I didn't write it down anywhere.
"Must be my… imagination."
"I see."
"Yeah."
"Sip… It really does taste bad."
"Oh, is that so?"
Kazusa holds the warm bowl firmly in her hands, complaining all the while.
This, too, is a scene I saw five years ago. These two events overlap to an uncomfortable degree.
…Including the fact that it's only her and me here.
"I don't even know what to say anymore."
"Shut up. If you don't know what to say then don't say anything."
Just like five years ago, Kazusa beautifully finishes my unimpressive dish without letting anything go to waste.
Then she obediently goes along with my order to go rest. She lies down on the bed and turns her back to me…
"You threw your pouch at a journalist… What part of that is 'losing' it? Tell me that beforehand."
Right now, she's blocking her ears as I lecture her.
"I only remembered once my head cooled down. At the time, my blood was boiling from anger…"
"That's the actual problem. Can't you do something about your way of treating others?"
"I'm a pianist. It's not my job to talk to people."
"Being a celebrity is part of being an artist. You wouldn't be able to get anywhere if people didn't take an interest in you."
"But that woman! She's awful. She's shameless. She almost reminded me of you!"
"Don't you think that… she just lost her temper because you kept giving her the cold shoulder, even though she's doing her best?"
As the receiver of baseless slander, I strike back at her without losing my temper in the slightest.
"But I've never been treated this way before, and I've only been in Japan for a week… Would it kill them to be a bit kinder?"
"If you're kinder to them, then they'll be kinder to you."
"I doubt such common logic would work on them. Just earlier, one of them came to my hotel room door with a camera. Don't they know they're causing problems for the hotel too?"
"…That sounds a bit rough, but I can't disparage people in the same industry as me like you can. I am fully aware of how hard they are working."
"See? In the end, your opinion is nothing more than a conflict of interest."
"Everyone cares about those in the same circle as them. It's the community that's the closest to them."
At that moment alone, I realize I'm getting goosebumps at my own words.
"Those words don't resonate with me at all… considering your relationship with your mother is worse than mine."
"…That's five year old information."
"So does that mean you've made up now? Like you forced me to."
My emotionless words were seen through by Kazusa.
Why would she remember my family circumstances from five years ago? Something so minor.
"See? Take a person who forces his own opinions on others yet can't do anything about himself and you've described Kitahara Haruki."
"It's pathetic to gloat about winning because of a specific case."
"Your empty lectures are even more pathetic. It's all either truisms or moralising without any basis in personal experience. It's lecturing for the sake of lecturing."
"That's obvious. I haven't lived long enough yet for my life experience to permeate my words."
"Are you going after me now?"
"I may live by the book, but by obeying every rule in the book, I believe I can accumulate experience."
"That's why you'll never be successful. You follow the mindset of everyone around you, so you never manage to break past them."
"What of it?"
"You might be able to climb the ranks of a company like that, but you'll never reach the top."
"Being at the top doesn't automatically make you happy, you know?"
"For example?"
"There is happiness in being with a person who can 'break past,' and helping them on the way up."
"Is that… what you want?"
"…It's just a common viewpoint."
That's…
…Not something I should have said to a genius who did manage to break past.
"Hey, Kazusa… You have changed less in these five years than me, don't you think?"
"Shut up… For how many hours do you have to lecture me before you're satisfied, Haruki?"
At that question, I look up at the clock to see that an hour has actually passed.
"Be a bit more honest."
"Like hell I can."
"Why not…? There's no point in being so stubborn."
"…Because if I did, things would end really badly."
"You are a good person at heart. There's no need to put on such a harsh front…"
"…Shut up already. It's time to be quiet now. I'm sleepy."
"You're free to fall asleep, and I'm free to continue talking."
"…Annoying."
"Good night, then."
"Hmph."
"If you remain the way you are now, what will you do if Youko-san can't be there to help?"
"I don't know how it was in the past, but right now you're clinging to her, aren't you? You're being raised by a really overprotective mother, aren't you?"
"I do think that you have a powerful charm that makes people want to go the extra mile to preserve your talent as a pianist."
"But you know, if you rely on that goodwill and leave everything bothersome to your mother, won't playing the piano be the only thing you do?"
"Nn…"
"In the past, you wrongly believed that you were abandoned. Youko-san herself felt responsible for that, and for the past five years, she's done something… that you could say is her way of atoning."
"Nhm…"
"But you know, it's about time… you paid her back for her kindness, don't you think?"
"…Nmmh."
"Isn't becoming independent the easiest and most effective way of showing filial piety to your parents?"
"…Mmn… Zzz…"
"I'm really jealous, to be honest…"
I already know Kazusa is asleep.
But unable to keep the words from spilling out of my mouth, I continue my annoying lecture toward the sleeping Kazusa.
If I kept this up, Kazusa would have gotten sick of me, given me a bitter laugh and exclaimed that everything has become ridiculous.
She would go back to being the Touma Kazusa from five years ago; a mere classmate and the girl I had a one-sided crush on.
Of course, that's a wish far too extravagant, and far too cruel.
"I got your address from Kaiousha… She's in there, right?"
"She is, but…"
It's 2 PM.
Carrying the pouch that Kazusa lost in her hands, Touma Youko came to my apartment herself.
For someone coming to pick up their daughter who didn't return, she seems awfully calm.
"It seems that my daughter caused you a lot of inconvenience last night…"
If anything, she's acting as if her daughter being here is the most natural thing in the world.
"Just so you know, I haven't done anything."
"I see… Poor thing."
…Who is she referring to?
"In any case, I'll go inside. Ah, also I'll take it with four sugar cubes and plenty of milk."
"…Are you talking about coffee, or black tea?"
"Ah, I'm sorry. I'll have coffee. If it's of the instant variety, I'd like half a spoon."
"I'll go boil the water, so give me a minute…"
That was not what she should have apologized about… These two really are mother and daughter.
"Anyway, is my idiot of a daughter… eh?"
"I'm sorry. I woke her up when I saw you were coming but…"
"Nhm… nh… fuu… haah…"
Youko-san looks at Kazusa lying sprawled on the bed in bewilderment.
"For how long has she been like this?"
"About twelve hours, I think. She had a slight fever, so I made her go to sleep as soon as she finished eating."
Setting aside the amount of time I lectured her, that is.
"She ate too?"
"Only porridge, and some… dessert?"
Without any concern to me screaming with my hands over my eyes, she ate all of the jam in my fridge…
"I give up… I really give up…"
"Youko-san?"
Youko-san changes her bewildered expression into some exaggerated European gesture, by lamenting with both her hands raised and spread open.
What is she so bothered about? Is Kazusa bad at waking up? …Like Setsuna is?
"And you dare say you don't belong in Japanーthat this is outside of your territory? Your mother is utterly embarrassed."
"Um…"
"What's up with this tranquil face of yours? …Maybe I should scribble on it. Guitar-kun, do you have a sign pen, one of those oil-based ones?"
"I do, but I won't give it to you."
After that, Youko-san kept staring at Kazusa's sleeping face, mumbling complaints along the way.
But Kazusa showed no signs of waking up, and Youko-san didn't show any intention to wake her up.
"Here's your sugared water… I mean coffee."
"Thank you… sip… hey, this tastes rather bitter."
Like mother, like daughter, truly.
"But still, it has been a while. Two weeks, perhaps?"
"Indeed."
Though compared to the five years before that, this is hardly worth mentioning.
"Ooh, so this is your castle, Guitar-kun… A bit cramped, don't you think?"
"…I'm just a regular employee."
"Oh, I found Guitar-kun's guitar. Let me borrow it for a second."
"Sure…"
"Ooh, an acoustic. Hmm… perhaps 10000 yen at most?"
"It was more expensive than that… 15000 yen."
The things I want to lecture her on increase by the minute, but I know she has no ill intent. She's just a little arrogant…
No, wait a second.

When I started playing the guitar five years ago and also half a year ago, I became painfully aware of the skill difference between me and a certain delinquent classmate, and it was a rather humiliating experience…
Our current situation is no more and no less than what happened back then…
"Haah, that must've been the first time in ten years… There is no trace of my original ability left."
I've had enough of this family. How much despair must they bring upon us normal people until they are satisfied?
"It seems you haven't used it much recently. You'll get rusty, Guitar-kun."
"My name is Kitahara. Enough with Guitar-kun already…"
Having her make our difference in skill so apparent feels like some kind of humiliation fetish…
"Come to think of it, perhaps this is causing a nuisance to your neighbor. Make sure to apologize to them later, okay?"
"It's fine. That room is vacant right now."
She has no intention of apologizing herself…
"Ah, I see, that's good… That's very good."
"…Fuu… Haah… Mnnn…"
…Despite Youko-san's showy guitar performance, Kazusa still showed no signs of waking up.
"Fuu… Haah…"
"…Hey."
"What is it?"
Youko-san speaks to me with her gaze still focused on Kazusa's sleeping face.
"They told me you refused the exclusive coverage of Kazusa."
"…It's too much responsibility for me."
"Kazusa wouldn't let anyone else take that responsibility, though."
"In that case, there's no need to write such a personal article, is there?"
"Should someone who's a part of the mass media really be saying that?"
I understand that I'm mixing work with private affairs.
I'm thinking about my own convenience, and cowardly running for dear life.
But inside that self-interest, there is actually another feeling existing alongside, coming from a different direction.
"She doesn't want it either. And besides, she's popular enough as it is. There's no need to set up special coverage now…"
My desire to not betray Setsuna any further…
…And my desire to not put Kazusa any further into the spotlight. These all too egotistical feelings.
"As her promoter, I don't care what it's about, I just want to increase her popularity while she's still relevant."
"Like you, Touma Youko?"
"You're right. Be it a scandal or anything else."
Am I supposed to admire her… because her words come from experience?
"I wanted to shoot at least one commercial while we're in Japan, but she herself stubbornly refused…"
"That's because Touma Kazusa isn't Touma Youko."
"In what way?"
"Let's see… She dreads promoting her own brand; on top of talking very little, she's clumsy with her words, and her ability to convey her feelings to others is catastrophic…"
"…You hit the mark."
Without getting angry or laughing, Youko-san merely looks at me with an unusual expression.
…I think it was like this five years ago too, when we met for the first time.
"…The two of you are identical in a number of ways. Though there's also many ways that the two of you are completely different."
"Well, that's obvious. Only half of her blood comes from me after all. There's no way she's going to be the same person as me."
"What about her father…?"
"No comment."
"…I'm sorry. I went too far."
"I don't mind telling you if you accept the job we talked about, though."
"…No, I think I'll refuse after all."
"Do you dislike being around this girl that much?"
"It's not about the job, but your condition for it. You shouldn't talk so lightly about things like that. I'm sure she'd be hurt if she heard that."
"So, does that mean you weren't speaking lightly when you asked about her father?"
…She makes it look like she's talking with sincerity, but she never misses an opportunity to put me in a bind.
"Well, I understand. I take back my condition, but I still want you to think about doing the job one more time."
"Why is that? Why me…?"
"Because I want everyone to know the true Touma Kazusa."
"Like I said, why…?"
Even that "why" carries with it two different questions.
"Like you know yourself, this girl is easily misunderstood. At this rate, all of that will surface before long."
The first question is "Where's the need to show everyone her true self?"
"But, as you also know, she's very timid and easily hurt… At this rate, she'll break down before long."
The second question is "Why do I have to carry the burden of this task?"
"That's why I want you to show everyone. Show them the expressions she only shows you."
"Eh…"
"Show them the girl you know, the girl you've seen with your own eyes and whose charming qualities you've felt drawn to…"
"But that's…"
Why would I do something like that…?
"Show it to Touma Kazusa herself too."
Why do I have to show them such a precious thing? I've always kept it hidden for the sole purpose of no one seeing it.
"Can I rely on you?"
I couldn't possibly…
And I don't have the right either.
"You can see this job as your final farewell toward Kazusa. But even then, tell her something… reject her, for her own sake."
It's just as Youko-san says…
I still haven't rejected Kazusa, and she hasn't rejected me.
At the airport terminal, we embraced, cried, and kissed… and then Kazusa passed the gate with eyes filled with tears.
Ever since back then, and up until this very moment, we've never promised that the two of us needed to stop longing for one another…
"If Kazusa goes through with the concert in her current state, I'm sure it'll go terribly. That girl's incredibly homesick right now."
"That's not something that I can cure."
"Do you really believe that?"
"After all, Kazusa wants to return to Vienna…"
"Do you think her home is over there?"
This person is completely different from how she looks.
The Touma Youko that Kazusa thought up is beyond inaccurate.
"At any rate, think about it. I'll contact the editing department once again at the end of the week."
Touma Youko is an overprotective mother…
For her daughter's sake, she'll do anything without hesitation.
Without once considering the feelings of those she drags into her mess, or what happens to them.
"Well then, I'll be going now. Sorry for my intrusion."
"Ah, but Kazusa is still…"
"She has her wallet back now, so tell her to walk home using her own two legs once she wakes up, would you? She's not a child anymore."
"…Couldn't agree more."
"See you some other time… Journalist Kitahara."
Just when I thought she had stopped calling me Guitar-kun…
Youko-san came up with a new label for me, binding me to a new crucifix.
"Oh my, welcome back. You seem to be in a good mood for the first time in a while."
"What happened? What's with the long face?"
"Why would you spew such pointless things…?"
"Huh? What are you talking about?"
"About Haruki! Calling me an idiot daughter, timid, homesick and whatnot."
"So you were awake."
"I can't hear you. How about you speak your excuses more loudly?"
"You have a big mouth for a raccoon dog."
"You're the raccoon dog! Spewing nothing but lies!"
"…He bought all of it, you know?"
"And exclusive coverage to top things off!? You can't be serious! I wouldn't let the mass media follow me around, and certainly not Haruki…"
"Truth is, Kazusa, I'm going to become a bit busy from now on. It's about your concert, and our activities after that."
"…What about it?"
"I will be unable to follow you around for a while. That's why you need someone to take care of you."
"Don't tell me… that's what you told him…?"
"Well, I suppose it'll be alright usually. But if something were to come up…"
"That's not necessary. I can take care of myself."
"If you were toーfor exampleーget into a fight with a journalist, or lose something of value on the streets…"
"We need someone to lend you a hand for 'unlikely' events such as that."
"B-But then anyone would do, wouldn't it!? You could hire a temporary manager during our time in Japan."
"If my daughter was cooperative enough for anyone to suffice, I would have done that, wouldn't you say?"
"…The fact that you went completely silent at that statement is partially my own responsibility, though."
"…In any case, I don't need anything like that. Turn it down."
"Where are you going? What about breakfast?"
"Practice. I can't stand being around you."
"Ah, right, right. One more thing."
"What is it?"
"You'll check out tomorrow, so could you gather all your luggage before you go to sleep tonight? …I'm sure it's scattered all over the place right now."
"Why?"
"Because you're a real nuisance to the hotel… We can't have them house a person who always starts arguments."
"Then where will I go? The media will catch my scent immediately anyway."
"Somewhere very convenient and pleasant… and a place that will protect you from a lot of crises. I'm sure you'll like it."
"Like I said, where is it…?"
"W-W-What… did you just say!?"
"I expected you to react loudly, but it's refreshing to see a reaction that even exceeds my expectations."
"Y-You can't be serious!"
"It goes without saying that I'm very serious."
"W-W-Wha…What are you thinking!? H-H-His apartment!?"
"Ah, I'm sorry for bursting your bubble when you're so excited, but it's not actually his apartment. I rented the apartment right next to his that just so happened to be vacant."
"What have you done!?"
"Didn't I tell you? It's somewhere very convenient and pleasant… That applies to the convenience of his job as well."
"M-Mom… What were you thinking? There's something wrong with you…"
"You're the one there's something wrong with. Why are you getting so worked up about living next to someone? It's not like you're going to live together."
"Because, because that's… you know already, don't you?"
"Know what?"
"…In fact, you probably knew and you're just making fun of me, aren't you?"
"If that's what you believe, then don't ask for my agreement, because my answer isn't what you'll want to hear."
"Stop it, Mom… Think about others for a change… Think about the people important to me."
"Kazusa…"
"This isn't just an issue of my own feelings anymore. I can't be allowed to get close to him."
"Even though you called him to pick you up?"
"I won't do it again. I won't ever do it again…"
"…I believe that's the fifth time I've heard you say that. And each time you say it you only wear yourself out more. What a handful."
"Do you know what's the most important thing for me right now? It's for your concert here in Japan to succeed."
"Mom…"
"That's why for the time being, I have chosen a place where your heart can be at ease."
"That's, that's… not true."
"…Even if that solution is nothing but a short-lasting drug."
"At any rate, it's only for your stay in Japan. Once the concert is over, then…"
"What about the side-effects…?"
"…I understand. If you truly wish to say no, you can stay here. However, you can also use that apartment whenever you want."
"I'm not going."
"After all, I've already signed the contract for it. You can move in starting tomorrow, you know?"
"I just said I'm not going."
"What about your practice?"
"…I'll go do that."
"Then go. Don't forget to bring some soba when greeting your new neighbors, okay?"
"I am not going there, you hear me!?"
"Yes, yes."
"Haah…"
Kazusa, whom I brought home on Friday, didn't wake up until Sunday morning…
When she woke up and our eyes met, she immediately began hurling abuse at me, put on her clothes and left.
I suppose I can see that as her just hiding her embarrassment, but I'd like to teach her a thing or two about showing gratitude to the person who housed her and gave her food.
But in truth, the only time I was able to forget about the worries that have been plaguing me since yesterday was those ten minutes.
"Nh… haaaah."
I land on the bed, and take a deep breath.
Staying awake next to the sleeping Kazusa this entire time has finally caught up to my entire body.
No, I can't; I can't close my eyes…
If I close my eyes now, my entire weekend will have been nothing but looking at someone sleep, and sleeping myself.
"Mh… Fuu… Haah…"
I land on the bed, and take a deep breath.
And then I realize something I haven't noticed before. A scent that reaches the depths of my heart, but a scent different to the usual.
…The scent of Kazusa.
The bed smells like Kazusa.
Because Setsuna hasn't been here for a short while, her familiar, sweet and captivating scent is completely gone.
Ah, I can't. I have to close my eyes…
If I don't close my eyes now, I'll be sucked into the darkness of these thoughts again.
I'll go through the entire weekend not getting a wink of sleep.
"At this rate, she'll break down before long."
…No, it doesn't matter if my eyes are closed or not. In the end, everything repeats itself anyway.
When I collapse on the bed and resign myself to sleep, the ominous words of yesterday float up in my head again.
"If Kazusa goes through with the concert in her current state, I'm sure it'll go terribly."
Youko-san's predictions…
Please, stop it already. What is it you want me to do?
I have nothing to do with Kazusa anymore…
"That's why I want you to show everyone. Show them the expressions she only shows you."
…No, Youko-san told me exactly what to do.
She told me to do my job.
To accept my exclusive coverage of Kazusa. To be on her tail during her stay in Japan.
And…
"Reject her, for her own sake."
I'm sleepy. I can't sleep.
Kazusa stole all of my sleep. And in return, I was given all of her anguish.
Perhaps this, too, is part of Touma Youko's plan.
Compare the stable private life of a regular magazine reporter like me, with the emotional stability of a popular pianist who's about to hold a concert. Obviously, the latter is much more important.
…It may be something obvious, but even the regular magazine reporter has a life he needs to protect.
I pick up my cell phone, and look at my incoming call history.
…But in my twenty most recent calls, the name of the person I want to find doesn't exist.
Setsuna…
The reason I can't fall asleep tonight is because Setsuna isn't by my side.
Because the person I want to be with more than anyone isn't in my embrace.
Even when Kazusa was asleep, I kept worrying about Setsuna suddenly coming over…
But Setsuna never came.
The "someday" in her "I promise to call you someday" didn't refer to this week.
Even though I'm aware it's my fault, I can't stop myself from resenting her for it.
As I'm feeling disgusted by the ugliness of my own heart, the name "Ogiso Setsuna" appears on my screen before I know it.
Setsuna would stop me, wouldn't she?
Perhaps she will rebuke me. Perhaps she will start sulking. Perhaps she will cry over the phone.
And then I would panic. I'd tell her that I won't make her feel sorrowful ever again, or make some other exaggerated proclamation like I always do.
And then once again, we'd return to how we used to be. That dreamlike reality…
1. I want to hear Setsuna's voice.
2. I promised not to call her first.
I pressed the button. I broke my promise with Setsuna.
I swore to her that I wouldn't call her until she forgave me.
This isn't something beyond my control. I can make no excuses. Right now, I'm piling one awful action over another.
But even then, I want to hear Setsuna's voice. No, I'm in trouble if I don't hear her voice.
Hey, Setsuna…
It looks like even in Japan, I'm having to interview Kazusa.
It's apparently some kind of exclusive coverage. We'll mostly be alone together, for as long as she's in Japan.
That sounds bad, doesn't it?
Hey, Setsuna…
Stop me already. Lament over it. Chastise me over it.
Give me a reason to say no… a reason that isn't for Kazusa's sake, but for your sake, Setsuna.
"Well done, we'll wrap things up for today…"
"Eh? But I can still continue."
"Yeah, but… we've gone on for four hours now, without breaks too."
"We have?"
"You didn't notice…?"
"She has no limits when she starts singing, nothing new there."
"We have only a week until the real deal. Shouldn't we polish up this song before we call it a day?"
"There's really no need to force it. This is your first practice session, Setsuna-chan."
"But I can only participate in one more practice session until the performance…"
"That's our problem. We don't want to force that much pressure on you, Setsuna-chan…"
"I agree. I feel bad enough just making you take part. Thanks to Kyouichi and Katsuya, those two bastards…"
"It's fine. I really want to sing right now… because I have so many things I want to forget, and so many things I want to remember."
"But you're employed now… You have work tomorrow, don't you?"
"What's the problem? Setsuna said she wanted to do it, so let her sing until she's satisfied."
"Tomo… You look strangely happy."
"Oh, you think so? Perish the thought."
"Jeez… What an ill-natured fan. Or should we be calling this girl her manager?"
"Are you sure about her, Setsuna-chan? If you get too involved with this person, you'll be debuting in show business before you realize it."
"Ahaha, setting jokes aside… Come on, once more from the top."
"Yes, yes. I couldn't ask for anything better… Alright, let's go."
In the end, my childish desire to push the decision onto Setsuna didn't materialize.
I don't know if she chose not to respond, knowing who was calling her, or if she just didn't notice.
But the result is clear. My indecision has been denied.
It's an overbearing result telling me to bear the responsibility by myself.
"…Kitahara? What's the matter? Did something happen?"
"I'm sorry for calling you on the weekend, Hamada-san…"
"…No way. What should I do?"
"Setsuna?"
"…It's Haruki-kun."
"Ooh, isn't that nice? So this time he broke the silence."
"W-What happened, I wonder? He said he wouldn't call me first…"
"Could he be calling to break up with you?"
"Tomo!"
"Nh… Mhmm…"
I noticed Setsuna's missed call after waking up from a deep slumber… It's 4 AM on Monday.
But I didn't call her back, after all…
"I'll do it. Please put me in charge of Touma Kazusa's special feature article."
Because I have already lost my last line of defense. That being Setsuna stopping me.
After thinking about it thoroughly, I press the call button.
I can't be sure if I'll get an answer on a Sunday afternoon.
And unless it's about something urgent, it's somewhat of a breach of manners.
After all, what my call consists of is…
"…Kitahara? What's the matter? Did something happen?"
"I'm sorry for calling you on the weekend, Hamada-san…"
…Work talk, on a weekend.
"Are you at work right now?"
"No, I'm at home. And nothing bad has happened, either."
"Is that so? I'm actually in the middle of a barbecue right now. All my family around the same age have gathered."
"Ah, I'm sorry. I'll call you back."
"No, I don't mind if it's short. What is it?"
"Ah, yes, umm…"
I promised not to call Setsuna.
"I was supposed to give you this answer by the end of the week…"
"Oh, that? …If you're calling me about it on a weekend, does that mean I can expect a favorable answer?"
That's why I'll make the decision myself. I'll take all the responsibility.
Because…
1. It's for Kazusa's sake.
2. There's nothing to worry about.
"I'll do it. Please put me in charge of Touma Kazusa's special feature article."
"Haaah…"
The moment I hung up the call, all my strength left my body, causing me to collapse on the bed.
Is it because the source of my anguish was cleared up? Did a switch inside of me go off? Am I just annoyed at myself for actually doing it?
Yes, I actually did it…
I actually accepted spending over a month with Kazusa.
Like that, I have only planted another ticking time bomb, but somehow I feel nothing but a strange sense of peacefulness.
"Huaaaah…"
I land on the bed, and take a deep breath.
And then I am once again submerged in Kazusa's scent.
Normally, this bed has Setsuna's scent on the weekends, but today…
"Good night…"
I wonder who I directed that to…
"…Haah! Haah…"
"That's not it, that's not it… The only reason I can't fall asleep is because I slept too much last night."
"It's because mom said those things… being homesick… that's not it."
"After all, I have… nowhere to return to anymore…"
